headings.title: Mud flap requirements, specifications, and exemptions

headings.title: Meaning of dump truck
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Defines "dump truck" for this section as a truck whose contents can be emptied without handling via a hydraulically raised front platform discharging by gravity.

headings.title: Arrest-warrant bar, failure notices, and default judgment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2024 S.B. 754, et al.). headings.title: Discretionary waiver upon proof of corrected equipment violation

headings.title: Director's authority to evaluate vehicle lighting safety

headings.title: Revocation or suspension of lighting approval certificates

headings.title: Finality and registered-mail notice of director's decisions

headings.title: Prohibition on vision-obstructing raised passenger vehicle bodies

headings.title: Required bumpers, exemptions, rules, and height table

headings.title: Safety inspection disapproval for noncompliant vehicles
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Prohibits approving vehicles violating this section during safety inspections required under §§ 307.350–307.390.

headings.title: Class C misdemeanor penalty for knowing violations

headings.title: Window-tint limits, medical permits, and windshield prohibition

headings.title: Exemptions for stickers, recreational vehicles, and factory tint

headings.title: Chapter 536 rulemaking compliance and nonseverability clause

headings.title: Class C misdemeanor penalty

headings.title: Sirens and blue lights for fire, ambulance, and rescue vehicles

headings.title: Authorized red, red-and-blue, and amber-and-white warning lights

headings.title: Federal hazardous-materials compliance for commercial highway transport

headings.title: Physical-requirement exemption for May 13, 1988 intrastate chauffeurs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. headings.title: Out-of-service authority under North American uniform criteria

headings.title: Definitions of child restraint terms and driver

headings.title: Penalties, section 307.178 cross-reference, and dismissal upon acquisition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes (including § 3.060 renumbering footnote noting subsection "5" of § 307.178 was updated to "6" per S.B. 30, 2019). Sets an infraction penalty up to $50 plus court costs for violating subsection 2(1)–(3) with mandatory dismissal/withdrawal upon proof of acquiring a restraint or booster seat, and applies § 307.178(6) to subsection 2(4).

headings.title: Exemptions for public carriers and qualifying school buses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and source notes. Exempts public carriers for hire and students four years of age or older riding on school buses designed for 11 or more passengers meeting Missouri Minimum Standards under § 301.010.

headings.title: Commission public information program
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and source notes. Directs the Highways and Transportation Commission to initiate and develop a public information program promoting understanding and compliance.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 5 subsections (including 1(1)–(3) and 2(1)–(6)), L. 2006 history, and the § 3.060 renumbering footnote updating § 307.178(5) to (6) per S.B. 30, 2019, and verified all fingerprints. headings.title: Permitted shoulder operation for slower bicycles
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2005 H.B. 487 merged with S.B. 372). Permits a person operating a bicycle slower than the posted speed or traffic flow to ride under § 307.190 or on the adjacent shoulder.

headings.title: Direction of travel on roadways and shoulders
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires bicycles operated on a roadway or adjacent shoulder to travel in the same direction required for motor vehicles on the roadway.

headings.title: Meaning of roadway for sections 307.190 and 307.191
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Defines "roadway" for §§ 307.190 and 307.191 as the portion of a street or highway ordinarily used for vehicular travel, excluding the berm or shoulder.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections and L. 2005 history and verified all fingerprints. Checked § 307.190 cross-references, shoulder-riding option, direction-of-travel rule, and 'roadway' definition; retained all 3 titles.

headings.title: Bicycle rights, duties, and vehicle status

headings.title: Exemption from motor-vehicle, dealer, licensing, and financial-responsibility laws
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Exempts electric bicycles and their operators from motor-vehicle, ATV, off-road/off-highway vehicle, rental, dealer/franchise, registration, title, driver's license, and financial responsibility laws. Independent review revised title from 'insurance laws' to the exact statutory term 'financial-responsibility laws'.

headings.title: Manufacturer and distributor permanent labeling requirements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires manufacturers and distributors, beginning August 28, 2021, to affix a prominent permanent Arial >=9-point label showing classification number, top assisted speed, and motor wattage.

headings.title: Relabeling requirement after speed or engagement modifications
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Prohibits modifying an electric bicycle's motor-powered speed capability or engagement without replacing the subsection 3 label to show the new classification.

headings.title: Federal Consumer Product Safety Commission compliance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Requires electric bicycles to comply with federal bicycle equipment and manufacturing rules in 16 CFR 1512.

headings.title: Motor disengagement on stopping pedaling or braking
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Requires electric bicycle motors to disengage or cease functioning when the rider stops pedaling or applies the brakes.

headings.title: Permitted riding areas, path restrictions, and natural-surface trails
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7, including subdivisions (1)–(4), and history note. Permits riding where bicycles are allowed and on bike/multi-use paths, allows banning class 1 or 2 e-bikes on paths after notice and public hearing for safety or legal compliance, allows banning class 3 on paths, and excludes designated nonmotorized natural-surface trails subject to local or state agency regulation.

headings.title: Age limit and speedometer requirement for class 3 electric bicycles
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8, including subdivisions (1) and (2), and history note. Bars operators under 16 from operating class 3 electric bicycles while allowing under-16 passengers on passenger-designed models, and requires a miles-per-hour speedometer. Independent review revised title from informal 'e-bikes' to the statutory term 'electric bicycles' while retaining under-16 operator bar, passenger exception, and speedometer requirement.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 8 subsections (including 7(1)–(4) and 8(1)–(2)) and L. 2021 S.B. 176 history, and verified all fingerprints. headings.title: Driver's license requirement for operating motorized bicycles
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1980 H.B. 995 & 1051 §§ 2, 3 through A.L. 2010 H.B. 1540). Prohibits operating a motorized bicycle on Missouri highways or streets without a valid motor vehicle operator's license.

headings.title: Prohibition on federal interstate highway operation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Prohibits operating motorized bicycles on any public thoroughfare in Missouri designated as part of the federal interstate highway system.

headings.title: Class C misdemeanor penalty
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Deems violation of this section a class C misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections and 1980–2010 history and verified all fingerprints. Checked license rule, federal interstate ban, and class C misdemeanor penalty; retained all 3 titles.

headings.title: Required ATV safety equipment and competitive-event exception

headings.title: Infraction penalty
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (A.L. 2009 H.B. 683). Makes violating section 307.198 all-terrain vehicle equipment requirements an infraction.

headings.title: Meaning of electric personal assistive mobility device
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2002 H.B. 1270 and H.B. 2032). Defines "electric personal assistive mobility device" (EPAMD) for sections 307.205 to 307.211 by wheel layout, single-rider design, 750-watt electric propulsion, and under-20-mph speed.

headings.title: Permitted operating areas and chapter 304 pedestrian rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Permits operating EPAMDs on streets, highways, sidewalks, and bicycle paths, granting operators chapter 304 pedestrian rights and duties.

headings.title: Minimum operator age and mobility-disability exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Prohibits persons under age 16 from operating an EPAMD, except operators with a mobility-related disability.

headings.title: Roadway speed-limit restriction and crossing exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Limits EPAMD operation to roadways with speed limits of 45 mph or less while allowing crossings of higher-speed roadways.

headings.title: Municipal authority to impose additional EPAMD regulations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Authorizes cities and towns to impose additional EPAMD operating regulations within municipal limits.

headings.title: Biennial inspection mandate, exemptions, timing, and certificates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, including subdivisions (1)–(4) and continuation paragraph, and history note (L. 1967 p. 418 § 1 through A.L. 2019 S.B. 89). Mandates biennial §§ 307.350–307.390 safety inspections for registered § 301.010 motor vehicles, exempts 10-year/<150,000-mile vehicles (excluding rebuilt prior-salvage and § 307.380 vehicles), proportionately registered interstate vehicles (preserving voluntary and peace-officer DOT inspections), § 301.131 historic vehicles, and short-term >24,000-lb vehicles, and sets odd/even model-year timing, § 307.375 school-bus timing, 60-day/dealer 90-day windows, certificate display, and replacement rules.

headings.title: Unregistered travel to inspection stations and repair facilities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Authorizes operating a vehicle without current state registration by the most direct route between residence and an inspection station, and between the station and repair places for inspection purposes only.

headings.title: No reinspection solely for special or personalized plates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Bars requiring reinspection of an approved vehicle solely to obtain § 301.144 personalized plates or § 301.142 plates prior to current registration expiration.

headings.title: Infraction penalty notwithstanding section 307.390
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Deems violation of this section an infraction notwithstanding § 307.390.

headings.title: Inspection prerequisite and out-of-state or renewal exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, including subdivisions (1) and (2), and source notes (L. 1967 p. 418 § 2 through A.L. 1999 S.B. 19; effective 7-01-00). headings.title: Out-of-state inspection reciprocity for interstate commercial vehicles
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes. headings.title: Exemption for mid-year commercial license or gross-weight changes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes. Waives inspection certificates for currently registered § 301.010 commercial motor vehicles changing from local to beyond-local registration or changing licensed gross weight during the licensed period.

headings.title: Station permits, forms, inspected items, and road-test exclusion
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1967 p. 418 § 3 through A.L. 1999 S.B. 19; effective 7-01-00). Directs the Highway Patrol superintendent to issue station permits, instructions, forms, and certificates covering listed vehicle safety systems, and excludes road testing from inspection procedures.

headings.title: Station standards, inspector qualifications, and operating rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes. Directs the superintendent to prescribe station standards, equipment, inspector qualifications, inspection procedures under §§ 307.350–307.390, and station operating rules, barring approval until met.

headings.title: Station permit applications, inspector permits, and private stations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3, including subdivisions (1)–(5), and source notes. headings.title: Station supervision, permit suspension or revocation, hearings, and appeals
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4, including subdivisions (1)–(3), and source notes. headings.title: Nontransferable permits, official signs, and repair-choice posters
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1967 p. 418 § 4 through A.L. 2012 H.B. 1402). Bars assigning, transferring, or relocating station permits, mandates conspicuous posting, provides one free official sign (additional signs at cost), and requires displaying posters advising the public that repairs need not be made at the inspection station.

headings.title: Official certificate issuance, brake testing, and certificate prohibitions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Limits certificate issuance to official forms after complete §§ 307.350–307.390 safety inspections, allows visual or computerized brake testing, prohibits unauthorized transfer of certificates, and prohibits knowingly possessing illegally purchased, stolen, or counterfeit certificates or stickers.

headings.title: Authority to require station reports
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Authorizes the Highway Patrol superintendent to require reasonably necessary station reports on furnished forms to administer §§ 307.350–307.390. headings.title: Twenty-day defect correction window and owner repair-choice notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. headings.title: Maximum inspection fees, free reinspections, and repair estimates

headings.title: Certificate fee, Highway Patrol Inspection Fund, and transfers

headings.title: Sticker refunds on station closure and annual sticker exchanges

headings.title: Class C misdemeanor penalty notwithstanding section 307.390
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Makes violating this section a class C misdemeanor notwithstanding § 307.390.

headings.title: Mandatory station liability insurance for inspection damage
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note. Requires inspection station owners or operators to maintain liability insurance at all times covering possible vehicle damage during inspection.

headings.title: Highway patrol school bus spot inspections at any time

headings.title: Class C misdemeanor penalty notwithstanding section 307.390

headings.title: Post-accident police-directed inspections and seller pre-sale inspections
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1967 p. 418 § 8 through A.L. 2021 S.B. 49; 1990 Viene v. Concours Auto Sales, Inc. annotation stating "as is" sales do not waive inspection requirements). Requires reinspection before highway use when police direct after an accident, and requires seller-paid full inspection of used § 307.350 vehicles immediately prior to sale regardless of any current certificate.

headings.title: Exemptions for junk, salvage, auction, and dealer sales
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes (including Viene annotation). Exempts sales for junk, salvage, or rebuilding, public auctions, and dealer-to-dealer sales, requires a Highway Patrol-prescribed purchaser affidavit for junk/salvage/rebuilding purchases, and bars re-registration of such vehicles until inspected and approved.

headings.title: Infraction penalty notwithstanding section 307.390
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes. Deems violation of this section an infraction notwithstanding § 307.390.

headings.title: Default misdemeanor penalty for sections 307.350 to 307.390
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1967 p. 418 § 10 through A.L. 2010 H.B. 1540; cross-reference to § 304.570 general penalty for §§ 307.020–307.295). Makes violating §§ 307.350–307.390 a misdemeanor punished as provided by law (subject to specific section-level overrides such as infractions or class C misdemeanors).

headings.title: Non-officer motor vehicle inspectors, summons authority, and training
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes. Authorizes the Highway Patrol superintendent to assign qualified non-officers as motor vehicle inspectors to enforce §§ 307.350–307.390 and §§ 643.300–643.355 with limited uniform complaint/summons authority after completing superintendent-approved training.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections, 1967–2010 history, and § 304.570 cross-reference note, and verified all fingerprints. Checked §§ 307.350–307.390 default misdemeanor penalty and non-officer motor vehicle inspector enforcement/summons authority for §§ 307.350–307.390 and §§ 643.300–643.355; retained both titles.

headings.title: Federal commercial-vehicle rules, hazmat inspections, and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, including subdivisions (1) and (2) and the exception continuation in subdivision (2), and history note (L. 1984 H.B. 1410 through A.L. 2013 H.B. 103). Incorporates 49 CFR Parts 390–397 for intrastate/interstate CMVs, authorizes Highway Patrol cargo-area hazmat inspection on reasonable grounds, authorizes DPS safety rules requiring safe maintenance and accident reporting, and exempts intrastate <=60,000-lb solid-waste and <=42,000-lb "F"-plate farm vehicles from the remainder of this section unless carrying hazmat.

headings.title: Intrastate chauffeur physical-requirement exemption and minimum driver ages
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Exempts intrastate drivers licensed by Missouri as chauffeurs on May 13, 1988 from 49 CFR Part 391 Subpart E physical requirements, and allows intrastate CMV operation at age 18+ except age 21+ for transporting hazardous materials.

headings.title: Out-of-service authority under North American uniform criteria
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Permits placing noncompliant commercial motor vehicles and drivers out of service under CVSA and U.S. DOT North American Uniform Out-of-Service Criteria. Independent review revised title from 'uniform federal criteria' to reflect joint CVSA and U.S. DOT North American Uniform Out-of-Service Criteria and permissive 'may be placed out of service'.

headings.title: Hours-of-service exemption for emergency utility restoration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Exempts intrastate vehicles and drivers of public utilities, rural electric cooperatives, and public service organizations from 49 CFR Part 395 driver hours rules while restoring defined essential utility services (electric, gas, water, telephone, sewer) during emergencies.

headings.title: Intrastate weight exemption with hazmat, passenger, and inspection limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5, including subdivisions (1)–(3) and the inspection-authority preservation sentence in subdivision (3), and history note. Exempts intrastate property-transporting CMVs <=26,000 lbs GVWR/GCWR from 49 CFR Parts 390–397 except non-covered-farm hazmat vehicles, >=16-passenger vehicles, and covered farm vehicles carrying 49 CFR 100–180 placarded hazmat, while preserving DPS-designated inspection authority.

headings.title: Class B misdemeanor penalty for statutory or rule violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Makes violating any provision of this section or any rule promulgated under it a class B misdemeanor.

headings.title: Chapter 536 rulemaking compliance and nonseverability clause
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Subjects rules under this section to chapter 536 and § 536.028 and declares nonseverability, voiding rulemaking authority and rules proposed or adopted after August 28, 2009 if legislative review powers are held unconstitutional.
